# Overmind vs. letta-ai/claude-subconscious

Same genre — a background observer that whispers into Claude Code — but different bets.

## What they share
- Session transcript → background agent → whispered guidance back into the next prompt.
- Persistent memory across sessions.
- No writes to CLAUDE.md; context is injected.
- Designed to stay quiet most of the time.

## Where they diverge

| | **Overmind** | **claude-subconscious (Letta)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Opinionated adherence monitor — 7 named workflow standards (explore-before-code, review-before-push, issues-for-future-work, etc.) | Generic observer — learns prefs, tracks project context, surfaces patterns |
| **Infra** | Fully local: Kuzu graph file, Claude CLI for eval | Letta Cloud account (or self-hosted Letta server) |
| **Memory model** | Temporal knowledge graph (Graphiti + Kuzu) — typed entities (Decision, Feedback, Request, Attempt, Suggestion) with timestamps | 8 named memory blocks, agent-managed, diffed between prompts |
| **Integration** | Skill + Python package spawning `watch.py`; injects via Monitor/notification | CC plugin with 4 hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop |
| **Agent's tools** | Read-only text: sees only user+assistant messages | Read/Grep/Glob/web_search on transcript; optional full tool access incl. `Task` |
| **Eval model** | Sonnet via `claude -p` (piggybacks on CC auth); gpt-5.4-mini for Graphiti | Configurable Letta-hosted agent; default `zai/glm-5` |
| **Patience** | Explicit: 3-8 turn debounce + 10s quiet + self-correction grace + no-repeat | Style-only ("observational, concise"); no documented mechanism |
| **Scope** | Per-project graph | One agent brain shared across all projects |
| **Two-way** | One-way (can't see tool outputs) | Two-way — CC can address Sub directly |

## Honest read

Letta is the more ambitious system — their Sub can actually explore the codebase while thinking, spawn sub-agents, run across projects. You're building a narrower, sharper tool: workflow enforcement with temporal recall, no vendor, no cloud.

The asymmetry to note: Letta's Sub sees tool outputs (it has Read/Grep itself). Overmind explicitly doesn't — noted as a limitation in your README. That's the biggest capability gap. Their hook fan-out (PreToolUse mid-workflow updates) is also tighter than Monitor-based injection — worth stealing if latency becomes a complaint.

Where you're genuinely ahead: the debounce + self-correction grace + no-repeat triad is a real patience discipline that their "be observational" prompt doesn't match. And the typed temporal graph gives you time-aware recall ("Alexey said this on 2026-04-01") that their memory blocks collapse into prose.

## Injection — Overmind vs Letta

**Overmind**: one path, async, stdout-as-notification.

- Skill tells Claude to launch `watch.py <session.jsonl>` via Claude Code's **Monitor** tool
- Monitor streams the child process's stdout — each line becomes a system notification to the main agent
- `watch.py` tails the session JSONL directly, evaluates in the background, and `print(thought, flush=True)` at `watch.py:246` when a concern survives the grace cycle
- No hooks, no `additionalContext`, no tagged blocks — the thought arrives as a plain notification line mid-conversation whenever Overmind decides to speak

**Letta**: four CC hooks, tagged XML blocks, two injection surfaces.

| Hook | Timing | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | Registers conversation; cleans legacy `<letta>` from CLAUDE.md |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | Before each user prompt | stdout → wrapped in `<letta_message>`, `<letta_memory_blocks>`, or `<letta_memory_update>` (diff) |
| `PreToolUse` | Before each tool call | Returns `additionalContext` if memory changed mid-workflow |
| `Stop` | After assistant reply | Async fire-and-forget: dumps transcript, spawns detached SDK worker |

### The structural difference

| | Overmind | Letta |
|---|---|---|
| **Trigger point** | Anytime (push model — emits when ready) | Only at hook boundaries (pull model — CC asks for context) |
| **Delivery channel** | Monitor stdout stream → notification | Hook stdout → `<letta_*>` tagged XML in prompt context, plus `PreToolUse.additionalContext` |
| **Shape** | One-line plain-text thought | Structured blocks: full dump first turn, diffs after |
| **Latency** | 15-30s after the event (your README) | Bounded by hook (5-10s) or next prompt |
| **Back-channel** | None — CC can't reply to Overmind | Two-way — CC can address Sub; Sub answers on next sync |
| **State on disk** | Kuzu graph + session logs | `conversations.json` mapping + temp logs |

### Honest read

Their hook model buys things you don't have: a **PreToolUse injection** that can catch a misstep between "I'll run rm -rf" and the actual call, and a **structured memory diff** so the model sees what changed, not just the latest snippet. Your Monitor-push model buys one thing they don't have: freedom to speak **mid-turn**, not only at hook boundaries.

If you wanted to close the gap, the cheapest move is adding a UserPromptSubmit hook that drains any pending Overmind thoughts into the next prompt as a tagged block — you'd keep push-timing but gain guaranteed delivery and a place to inject recall context on every turn.
